summary: The code is syntactically valid, imports are correct, and the simulation components are broadly implemented with reasonable logic and error handling. However, the default runtime behavior performs an expensive calibration (random search) with a large population and multi-day horizon, which is likely to cause timeouts in sandboxed execution. There are also a few minor implementation/performance concerns.

issues.description: Default run triggers RandomSearch calibration with budget=50 on a population of 5000 over ~30 days per trial, resulting in 50 full simulations. This is very likely to exceed time limits in a sandbox or CI environment.
issues.location: orchestrate() and Calibrator defaults; parse_args default --calibrator=random_search; Simulation.run called from evaluate_params() in calibration loop
issues.solution: Change the default calibrator to 'none' in parse_args, or set a much smaller default budget. Alternatively, automatically enable fast mode when SKIP_IO is true, and/or enforce a strict time budget or trial cap in calibrators even when FAST_MODE is false.

issues.description: Homophily rewiring constructs a full non-neighbor candidate list for each rewiring step, which is O(N) per step and can be expensive when many rewires are attempted.
issues.solution: Sample a small random subset of candidates instead of iterating over all N agents (e.g., 20-50 random candidates) or maintain a faster membership structure. This will reduce per-rewire cost from O(N) to O(1)-amortized.

issues.description: Parameter persistence ignores SKIP_IO, potentially writing files in environments where I/O should be avoided.
issues.solution: Guard file writes with the SKIP_IO flag, similar to other I/O operations in the code.

issues.description: Calibration loops only enforce a time budget when FAST_MODE is true; in non-fast runs there is no time capping.
issues.solution: Apply a time budget cap unconditionally, or scale it with budget/population size. For example, stop trials when elapsed time exceeds a specified limit.

issues.description: Setting os.environ['SKIP_IO'] inside orchestrate() does not affect the SKIP_IO module-level constant (already set at import).
issues.solution: Either rely solely on the module-level SKIP_IO or recalculate SKIP_IO after changing the environment variable. Alternatively, pass a runtime flag instead of relying on environment variable changes.
